label: Get the Job — Marketing
overview: The Get the Job — Marketing content helps advisors transition from basic tax compliance to high-value consulting. It is primarily strategic and communication in nature — a turnkey system equipped with communication templates, predictive modelling, and legal safeguards. Tools cover the full outreach lifecycle: automated prospect warming via quizzes and video links, portal invitations, staff training programs, crisis communication, and third-party legal agreements. Entry-level and suitable for all advisors. The seven materials below are sequenced by the four-step execution method: prepare the system, warm the prospect with a micro-step, invite and orient them, then formalise the engagement.

diagnostic_entry.primary_question: What stage of client outreach or marketing are you working on — generating new leads, inviting clients to the portal, training their staff, managing a crisis, or formalising a third-party relationship?

materials.name: 1st Response & Proposal Templates
materials.summary: Brings Agile Theory to advisory engagements by breaking a project into manageable sprints — Feasibility, Planning, Implementation — rather than asking for the whole thing upfront. For the owner it removes the risk of committing to a large, expensive project blind: a $5,000 feasibility stage taking about five hours of their time establishes the structural integrity first. For the advisor it sets clear expectations, secures paid work early, and positions them as a strategic partner reviewing the critical business functions.
materials.who_when: Prospects and existing clients enquiring about large projects or new advisory engagements.
steps: Introduce the engagement as three sprints — Feasibility, Planning, Implementation — rather than one commitment, so the client is deciding one step at a time.
Scope the feasibility sprint explicitly: about $5,000 and roughly five hours of the client's time, to assess structural integrity before any budget is finalised.
State what the feasibility sprint systematically reviews — Planning, Data Management, Marketing and the other critical business functions — so the client sees a method rather than an opinion.
Set expectations in writing before work starts, so the transition from feasibility into planning is a decision the client already understands.
Where the project involves sensitive operational data or reveals the firm's proprietary frameworks, put the Mutual Confidentiality Agreement in place at this feasibility stage, not later.

materials.name: Marketing Campaigns, Quizzes & Video Hyperlinks
materials.summary: Outreach assets that automate the approach and act as a micro-step between first contact and a formal meeting, using short videos and quick quizzes to open discussion on cash forecasting, business planning and growth fundamentals. For the owner they focus attention on a seasonal risk — the perfect storm of tax and the holidays — and let them test their assumptions in three minutes. For the advisor they generate qualified leads and prime a client for the theme of the meeting without heavy manual selling.
materials.who_when: Existing clients needing a nudge toward quarterly planning, and new prospects who need warming up before a sales call. The entry point for any advisor uncomfortable with direct selling.
steps: Identify the target list, then choose the asset that matches the theme you want the meeting to be about.
Embed a specific video hyperlink in your email signature — the Bags of Cash video for cash forecasting, for example — or send a targeted text containing the link.

Use the three online quizzes as the qualifying step: Growth Fundamentals, What's Applicable, and HR Maths. They take about three minutes and are designed to prime a prospect for the sales meeting that follows.

Run the seasonal campaign where it fits — the third-quarter outreach uses email and text scripts on cash forecasting and business planning to secure working capital reviews ahead of the holiday silly season.
Monitor the results to identify warm leads, then follow up by reviewing their quiz results with them rather than making a pitch.

materials.name: 90-Day Best Practice Training Outreach
materials.summary: A structured four-to-five-session training plan delivered over Zoom, teaching a client's own admin staff to use Xero properly. For the owner it means correct coding, sound transaction handling and monthly quality control — which is what prevents costly mistakes and surprise tax bills. For the advisor it pre-empts the birds-nest nightmares that otherwise have to be untangled at year end, and creates a revenue stream in its own right.
materials.who_when: Business owners using digital accounting software who have no formal bookkeeping training or an inexperienced admin team. Also the natural pivot when a client's underlying data turns out to be too messy for advisory work.
steps: Diagnose the data first — if the client's underlying records are messy, sell this before attempting any advisory engagement built on those numbers.
Schedule four to five Zoom sessions with the people who actually do the work, not the owner.
Cover software coding, transaction generation, and monthly quality control across the sessions.
Close off the 90 days formally, so the improvement is checked rather than assumed.
Price it as standard: $1,500 + GST for local traders, $1,800 + GST where the business trades internationally, billed in three monthly instalments to ease the client's cash flow.

materials.name: Crisis Management (COVID-19 Email & Phone Scripts)
materials.summary: A compassionate, structured way to reach clients during a lockdown, supply shortage or sudden downturn — three emails and two phone scripts. For the owner it models Good, Bad and Ugly revenue scenarios and gets them to the bank before the credit division is overwhelmed, then narrows their focus to one of three functions: Getting Organised, Getting the Job, or Doing the Job. For the advisor it demonstrates real value and empathy at no initial cost, which is what cements the relationship.
materials.who_when: All active clients facing a sudden economic downturn, lockdown or severe market disruption.
steps: Reach out early using the email templates — the point is contact and clarity, not a sale.
Model the Good, Bad and Ugly revenue scenarios with the client so the range is quantified rather than feared.
Move quickly on funding: help them prepare and approach the bank before credit divisions are swamped.
Narrow their attention to one of the three core functions — Getting Organised, Getting the Job, or Doing the Job — so a panicking owner has one thing to work on.
Follow up by phone using the scripts; the free help given here is what leads to paid programmes later.

materials.name: Portal Invitations & System Checklists ("Let the Software do the Lifting")
materials.summary: Invitation emails in three tones, from direct to conservative, paired with the internal checklists for building the client's portal account. The conservative version frames the software as a mental gym, which lowers the intimidation for a client who has never had a portal. For the owner it is 24/7 access to a single hub for meeting agendas, action plans and improvement templates; for the advisor it standardises onboarding and makes client engagement visible.
materials.who_when: New or existing clients moving onto the firm's advisory platform, and the internal staff who set those accounts up.
steps: Prepare the system before making contact — use the Xero API to mass-create the business entities in the portal.
Import each client's cash volatility and financial performance data so their dashboard is populated before they ever log in.
Tailor the Client Service Plan by hiding or locking the modules they do not need yet, so the first view is not overwhelming.
Send the invitation email in the tone that suits the client — direct through to the conservative mental gym framing.
Treat the release as a process rather than one event: email, then a text reminder, then a call within 48 hours to walk them through their first login and explain why it helps them.
Book and run the 15-minute orientation session over Zoom.

materials.name: Third-Party Collaboration & Legal Templates (Consent, Banker Login, NDA)
materials.summary: Formalises relationships with people outside the engagement. The Mutual Confidentiality Agreement protects intellectual property and sensitive financial information; the consent template lets an external advisor such as a banker see specified portal pages. For the owner it builds transparency with a lender and can speed up funding; for the advisor it protects proprietary methods and builds a referral relationship with bankers.
materials.who_when: Clients requiring bank loans, the external banking partners themselves, and prospects evaluating a custom software project where proprietary frameworks will be shared.
steps: Introduce the Mutual Confidentiality Agreement at the Feasibility stage — when sensitive operational data is about to be shared, or when the firm's proprietary consulting frameworks are being revealed.

Secure the client's formal consent through the external advisor consent email before any third party is given access, naming the specific pages they may see, such as the Covid-19 section and the Loan Estimator.
Send the banker the short registration email with their link to the platform.
Bring the banker into the client's exposure dashboard so the cash flow scenarios are visible to the lender.

Use the script that tells the banker you accept referrals for advisory work without requiring the client to leave their existing compliance accountant — that is what makes the referral safe for them to make.
Never share proprietary frameworks or client financial data with a third party before the agreement or consent form is in place.

materials.name: Website Blurbs & Messaging Plan
materials.summary: Ready-to-use copy that maps a homepage into bands — attention, problem, position, solution — together with a slide deck for planning the firm's global messaging and its timeline. For the owner visiting the site, it answers the question they actually arrived with, such as how much is enough, inside the first 7 to 20 seconds. For the firm it saves hours of copywriting and aligns website, blog and social content to the same target-market problems.
materials.who_when: Accounting firms revamping a website, aligning a team's marketing efforts, or building a communication timeline across marketing and seminar activity.
steps: Write the homepage in bands — attention, then problem, then position, then solution — rather than as continuous prose.
Answer the visitor's core question inside the first 7 to 20 seconds; that is the whole window you have.
Position the service range aspirationally using the ascension diagram, from Basic Accounting through to Legacy packages.
Use the messaging plan deck to identify the target market's problems and establish the core Concept Domains the firm speaks to.
Build the broad timeline for marketing and seminar activity from those domains, so social, blog and website work all point at the same problems.

advisor_guidance.sequence: Follow the 4-step outreach sequence: (1) Internal system preparation — set up client portals before contact. (2) Micro-step outreach — quiz or video link to warm the prospect. (3) Portal invitation and follow-up — invite and orient. (4) Formalise the engagement — use 1st Response, NDA, or consent forms as required.
advisor_guidance.entry_point: If you are uncomfortable with direct selling, start with the micro-steps (quiz links and video hyperlinks). These assets do the qualifying work for you — when you follow up, you are reviewing their quiz results, not making a cold pitch.
advisor_guidance.legal_protection: Never share proprietary frameworks or client financial data with a third party without the NDA or External Advisor Consent form in place. These are not optional — they are your legal protection.
